summary: Stepwise safe demote and telemetry capture after latency variance following optimizer config change
description: Issue summary: MedAssist reports increased 95p and 99p tail latency for text-generation routes after they enabled a combined optimizer profile (async batching + aggressive quantization + KV prefetch) during a controlled rollout on 2026-03-13. Impact: customer-facing API latency spikes causing several calls to miss SLOs and user-facing timeouts for workflows that require sub-500ms tail latency. Environment: prod (us-east), dedicated enterprise account, pinned model rw/gpt-large-1.2B-finetuned. Steps to reproduce: 1) Use customer's route and tenant config (attached snapshot) 2) Send steady traffic at customer's distribution (joined sample CSV) 3) Observe 95p/99p across 1 hour window and streaming disconnect counts. Observed behavior: after config flip at 2026-03-13T13:20Z 95p latency increased from ~310ms to ~920ms and 99p from ~620ms to ~2.1s. Error traces show increased queuing and occasional model-worker GC/eviction chatter. Expected behavior: modest tail regression for small latency gains; not SLO-violating. Attachments: customer's config snapshot, compressed pprof samples, APM traces, and traffic sample CSV.
investigation_notes: Summary of findings: - Timeline: config applied (optimizer profile id opt-ff32-agg-batch-kv) at 2026-03-13T13:20Z; latency jump aligned to rollout window. - Telemetry: batching histogram shows async_batch_size target increased from 4->12 for long sessions; KV prefetch hit ratio dropped for this tenant causing repeated cache misses and extra KV RPCs. - Quantization: quant fallback events logged for ~7% of requests (runtime fell back to higher-precision kernels under memory pressure). - Resource signals: GPU utilization stable, but host-side CPU and io_wait increased on several serving hosts processing this tenant. - Hypothesis: combined increase in async batching plus aggressive kv-prefetch unexpectedly changed request inter-arrival distribution, leading to larger per-batch assembly delays and cache churn; quant fallback amplified CPU/host latency and caused tail amplification. Dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood/internal/d/latency/tenant-MedAssist; trace example: https://apm.redwood/trace/9a7b3c
workaround: Immediate safe-demote plan executed as a staged operation: 1) Traffic-split 10% canary -> reduce async_batch_target to 6 and disable kv-prefetch for that canary route 2) Monitor 95p/99p and error-rate for 15 minutes 3) If improvement >30% at 95p, expand to 50% traffic-split and keep telemetry capture enabled 4) For remaining traffic, set per-route override to quant_profile: balanced (instead of aggressive). Implementation commands: - route override via Console > Routes > MedAssist-TextGen > Overrides - API: PATCH /v1/routes/{route_id}/overrides {"async_batch_target":6, "kv_prefetch":false, "quant_profile":"balanced"} 5) Keep snapshot of current optimizer profile (snapshot id saved) and do not purge until full validation. Monitoring hooks: 95p/99p, quant-fallback count, kv miss rate, host CPU iowait. Safety gates: auto-rollback to prior snapshot if 99p > 2s for two consecutive 5-min windows.
resolution_notes: In progress: support and SRE applied the staged demote for 10% canary at 2026-03-13T16:05Z per workaround. Early results: 95p for canary dropped from 910ms -> 380ms within 12 minutes; quant-fallback reduced to 1.1% from 7%. Customer agreed to expand to 50% at 2026-03-13T16:30Z. Next steps: - complete 50% expansion and re-evaluate after 30m - schedule controlled full rollout reversal if stable - prepare postmortem runbook entry and update optimizer profile recommendation for this workload to avoid simultaneous aggressive batching and kv-prefetch for long-session distributions. Follow-up action item: SRE to open INT ticket to add an automated preflight check that flags high kv miss rate when async_batch_target > 8.
